papers.title_en: Any-Rate: Half-Bit Multi-Precision LLM Quantization with Coded Bit-Planes
papers.authors: Hoonki Lee, Haechan Shin, Hyuntaek Jung, Yeonu Choi, Sangyeob Kim
papers.evidence: 单检查点半比特多精度大模型量化
papers.tldr: 嵌套多精度量化可从单一检查点按前导比特读出多档精度，但现有方法仅支持整数比特，相邻档位精度差距大且2比特退化严重。Any-Rate在2–4比特间以半比特步进并覆盖2–8比特，将部分位平面约束为8权重块上的扩展Hamming码字（每权重0.5比特），每行跨精度共享LUT并联合编码各精度。四个LLM上，2/3比特达多精度方法SOTA，2比特保留69% FP16精度，4比特与最佳相差1点内。解码速度接近现有内核，等精度下LPDDR能耗估计最多降27%。
papers.abstract_en: Nested multi-precision quantization derives multiple precisions from a single checkpoint by reading only the leading bits of each weight, which makes it attractive for on-device deployment under varying memory and energy budgets. However, existing methods offer only integer bits, leaving large accuracy gaps between adjacent precisions and severe degradation at 2 bits. To address this, we propose Any-Rate, which serves 2-8 bits from one checkpoint, in half-bit steps over 2-4 bits. Any-Rate restricts some bit-planes to extended Hamming codewords in 8-weight blocks (0.5 bits per weight), shares one LUT per row across precisions, and encodes all precisions jointly with a separate target for each, reducing the loss from sharing bit-planes. Across four LLMs, Any-Rate achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among multi-precision methods at 2 and 3 bits, keeping 69% of FP16 accuracy at 2 bits, and is within one point of the best at 4 bits. It decodes about as fast as existing kernels, and an LPDDR energy model estimates up to 27% less energy at equal accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/hoonki2002/Any-Rate.

papers.title_en: Integration of Vision-Language-Action Control for Autonomous Forklift Unloading with Limited Real-World Data
papers.evidence: 视觉-语言-动作模型直接生成叉车卸载控制动作
papers.tldr: 叉车在仓储物流中很关键，但现有自动化系统难以处理需要多步决策的复杂卸货任务，VLA模型虽在机械臂上广泛研究，却尚未用于叉车。本文用机器人操作数据预训练的VLA模型，结合9.38小时仿真数据和0.8小时真实演示（真实数据约占8%）迁移到叉车控制。四种模型变体共完成72次真机试验，系统在有限真实数据下仍能完成卸货。该工作验证了VLA用于自主叉车卸货的可行性，为低成本数据采集与仓储自动化提供参考。
papers.abstract_en: Forklifts play a critical role in warehousing and distribution, but existing automation systems remain limited in handling complex tasks that require sequential decision-making. Recently, vision--language--action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising approach for multi-step decision-making by directly generating control actions from visual observations and language prompts. Although VLA-based control has been extensively researched for manipulators, to the best of our knowledge, its application to forklifts remains unexplored. Therefore, this study demonstrates the integration of VLA control for an autonomous forklift unloading task with limited real-world data. Moreover, training VLA models typically requires large-scale datasets. As there is currently no public dataset for forklift operations, we use a VLA model pretrained primarily on robotic manipulator data and construct a training dataset via simulation, which can be scaled up at low cost. We then adapt the pretrained VLA model to forklift control using 9.38 h of simulation data and 0.8 h of real-world demonstrations, with the latter accounting for approximately 8% of the collected forklift data by duration. The integrated system was validated through 72 real-world trials across four model variants. The results show that the proposed system can accomplish an unloading task even with limited real-world data.

papers.title_en: Aegis-VLA: Reliability-Gated Action Refinement via a Trajectory World Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
papers.authors: Lennox Wei, Jiaqi Yao, Shixin Sun, Yuanzheng Zhang, Jianhua Han, Meng Tian, Shaohui Liu, Wangmeng Zuo
papers.evidence: 面向动态物体操作的世界模型引导VLA
papers.tldr: 动态物体操作要求推理与执行中持续保持时空对齐，但准确预测未来并不等于应修改动作。Aegis-VLA用轨迹世界模型预测目标运动与位置不确定性，并以差异引导动作精修和可靠性门控筛选修正。模拟DOM基准1800次试验成功率达56.72%，比复现DynamicVLA基线45.44%高11.28个百分点。该框架仅约2.45M可训练参数，为动态操作提供可门控修正方案。
papers.abstract_en: Dynamic object manipulation requires maintaining spatial and temporal alignment with targets that continue to move during inference and execution. Although future prediction can inform action correction, an accurate forecast does not establish whether modifying an existing action would be beneficial. We present Aegis-VLA, a world-model-guided vision-language-action (VLA) framework that generates predictive action corrections and separately determines whether and how strongly to apply them. A Trajectory World Model combines kinematic extrapolation with learned residual dynamics to predict object motion and estimate positional uncertainty. Discrepancy-Guided Action Refinement uses differences between history-only and base-action-conditioned end-effector forecasts to propose bounded arm corrections. A Reliability Gate learns when to admit corrections based on demonstration-relative improvements over base actions, and regulates their application during inference using predictive uncertainty and anticipated object--end-effector proximity. Rejected corrections preserve the corresponding base actions. Aegis-VLA introduces only approximately 2.45M trainable parameters. On the simulated Dynamic Object Manipulation (DOM) benchmark, Aegis-VLA achieves 56.72\% success over 1,800 evaluation trials, exceeding our reproduced DynamicVLA baseline of 45.44\% by 11.28 percentage points.

papers.title_en: CoTacWAM: Joint Modeling of Vision and Touch for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Lei Jin, Yiding Ma, Zhuohang Li, Jiachen Liu, Zibo Zhu, Kairui Liu, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li
papers.evidence: 融合腕部视觉与触觉的机器人操作策略学习
papers.tldr: 机器人操作中视觉与触觉信号异质，现有策略难以在缺失输入时保持稳健，也难以统一利用两种接触证据。CoTacWAM 联合建模手腕视觉与触觉的共享接触语义，同时保留各模态独有信息，形成覆盖不同输入组合的交互联合描述，并支持预测式动作学习与失败检测后的自主重试。四个真实任务显示其操作性能优于评估基线，对局部观测缺失更稳健，自主重试还能带来额外增益。
papers.abstract_en: We present CoTacWAM, a world-action model that learns shared contact semantics between wrist vision and touch, achieving the best observed performance in our nominal manipulation and missing-input evaluations. The two modalities observe the same local interaction through different signals: wrist images reveal nearby geometry, while touch records physical contact. Our approach connects their common contact meaning while preserving the evidence unique to each modality, giving the policy a joint description of interaction across available input combinations. This representation supports predictive action learning alongside head-view scene context and conditions corrections after an independent detector confirms a failed attempt. Experiments across four real-world tasks demonstrate improved manipulation performance over the evaluated baselines, robustness to missing local observations, and further gains from autonomous retries.

papers.title_en: Beyond Natural-Language Instructions: Temporal Logic as a Task Language for VLA Models with Visual-Logical Fusion
papers.authors: Zezhi Liu, Jingwen Sun, Hongjin Chen, Shaojie Ren, Peiyan Tu, Xin Jin, Zhibo Chen
papers.evidence: 以时序逻辑任务规范条件化机器人动作的视觉-语言-动作框架
papers.tldr: 机器人任务常含对象关系、逻辑依赖与时序约束，自然语言指令难以显式表达这些结构。TL-VLA用时序逻辑作为任务语言，结合类型图编码器与视觉-逻辑融合，将连续动作条件化于任务规范和当前观测，并通过TL感知预训练对齐语义与结构。在CALVIN ABC→D、LIBERO-10/Mem和Panda规划规范上，多项指标优于NL及FAST/Qwen基线。结果表明显式逻辑任务条件与可迁移TL表征能提升VLA动作学习。
papers.abstract_en: Robotic tasks combine object relations, logical dependencies, and temporal requirements, which robot planning and industrial control commonly specify in temporal logic (TL). We introduce TL-VLA, a vision--language--action framework that replaces natural-language task instructions with temporal logic, making this spatiotemporal structure explicit. A typed graph encoder and visual--logical fusion condition continuous actions on the task specification and the current observations. To prepare a general vision--language backbone for this interface, we develop TL-aware robot pretraining with separate semantic and structural readouts: a frozen language teacher aligns task semantics, the structural readout encodes TL syntax to support complex, long-horizon tasks, and autoregressive action prediction connects the graph representation to robot behavior. Downstream policies inherit the pretrained backbone and TL encoder and learn new fusion and action modules. On CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, our TL-aware initializer reaches \textbf{3.800} average chain length and \textbf{62.3\%} five-task success, compared with 3.578 and 54.5\% for a FAST initializer pretrained on the same data and 3.485 average chain length for a Qwen+NL baseline. On LIBERO-10, TL-aware initialization improves success from \textbf{91.2\% to 95.8\%}. On LIBERO-Mem, our policy reaches \textbf{65.0\%} success without observation history, compared with 45.0\% for a Qwen+NL reference. On held-out Panda planning specifications, it reaches \textbf{59.6\%} at Success@256 over three generation seeds, versus 48.4\% for Qwen+TL and 37.0\% for Qwen+NL. These results support explicit logical task conditioning and transferable TL-aware representations for robot action learning.

papers.authors: Xuewu Lin, Jiahao Wang, Jiawei Li, Mengdi Li, Zhengmao Sun, Yiwei Jin, Hongyu Xie, Zhengyang Feng, Kun Wu, Zihao Chen, Lianzhou Zhang, Lichao Huang, Zhizhong Su
papers.evidence: 面向跨具身机器人操作的视觉-语言-动作策略
papers.tldr: 跨机器人本体的操作策略难以共享动作空间与运动学表示。HoloBrain-0.5 统一 URDF 关节轴、坐标系与工具中心点，并以共享三维运动学图表征，提供扩散连续策略和残差FSQ离散策略，用超1万小时真实、仿真与人类数据预训练。离散策略在六项仿真中平均成功率56.77%，优于连续策略49.71%；连续策略后训练后在七任务达94.52%，超过π0.5的86.25%。该工作展示了跨本体VLA的可扩展迁移与少样本适配能力。
papers.abstract_en: We present HoloBrain-0.5, a family of vision-language-action (VLA) models for manipulation across robot embodiments. The policies plan in a shared action space using robot state, kinematic structure, and calibrated camera observations. We standardize joint axes, coordinate frames, and tool-center points in robot descriptions (URDFs) and encode their kinematic graphs in a shared 3D representation. HoloBrain-0.5-Continuous generates action chunks by diffusion, while HoloBrain-0.5-Discrete uses residual finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and delayed autoregression. We pretrain both policies on over 10,000 hours of real-robot, simulation, and human-manipulation data spanning 15 embodiment categories.   Across six closed-loop simulation settings, the discrete policy converges faster and reaches a higher mean success rate than the continuous policy (56.77% vs. 49.71%). On seven real-robot tasks, it achieves a mean progress score of 87.76% without task-specific post-training. After post-training, the continuous policy outperforms $π_{0.5}$ on the seven-task benchmark (94.52% vs. 86.25%) and an 11-task dual-arm benchmark (79.07% vs. 69.41%). The discrete-initialized continuous policy transfers five tasks zero-shot from Piper to Piper-X, scoring 63.28% on average. With target-robot demonstrations, the continuous policy scores 89.2% on Franka Panda and 92.94% on a mobile dual-arm platform. Although pretraining includes no Unitree G1 data, post-training with limited G1 demonstrations yields a mean progress score of 70.24% across three humanoid tasks, compared with 11.00% for $π_{0.5}$.

papers.title_en: Dynamic Task Update Benchmark (DTU-Bench): Evaluating Runtime Task Adaptation in Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Yanran Jiang, Cécile Paris, Dana Kulić, Leimin Tian
papers.evidence: 面向机器人操作的视觉-语言-动作策略评测
papers.tldr: 现有VLA策略在固定指令操作基准上表现优异，但执行中指令变更后的适应能力缺乏评测。作者提出DTU-Bench，基于LIBERO覆盖40种任务修订、7类更新和3个执行阶段，对比执行前与执行中改指令，并测试13种VLA配置。结果显示原始任务成功率95.8%，执行中改操作对象仅1.6%；简单释放物体并回臂控制器可将π0.5从2%提至38%、DM0.5从8%提至48%，但会带来非预期物体运动。该基准揭示固定指令评测与任务成功率指标会掩盖运行时适应缺陷。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies perform well on fixed-instruction robotic manipulation benchmarks, but their ability to adapt to instruction changes during execution remains understudied. We introduce the Dynamic Task Update Benchmark (DTU-Bench), evaluating 40 task revisions across seven update types and three execution stages using LIBERO, a simulated robotic manipulation benchmark. We compare performance when a new instruction is given before execution starts versus during execution, and examine whether the new task instructions are followed. Across 13 representative VLA configurations, average task success is 95.8% on the original object-manipulation tasks, compared with only 1.6% when the instruction changes which object to manipulate during execution. Controlled diagnostics show that policies often complete the original task before the updated one, and that their responses depend on the robot's physical state. We further test whether a simple scripted controller that releases the grasped object and moves the arm back helps robots respond to instruction changes. This improves success from 2% to 38% for π0.5 and from 8% to 48% for DM0.5, but can cause unwanted object motion. These findings reveal limitations that fixed-instruction benchmarks and task-success metrics alone can overlook in evaluating robotic manipulation. Project page: https://dtu-bench.github.io/

papers.title_en: JEPA-Tuner: From Predictive Fine-Tuning to Asynchronous Execution of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Jingxiang Qu, Tian Xie, Youngjin Hong, Changhyun Choi, Yang Katie Zhao, Yi Liu
papers.evidence: 面向视觉-语言-动作模型的预测式微调与异步执行
papers.tldr: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在具身交互中执行动作会改变后续观测与机器人状态，但标准动作监督微调并未显式利用这种动作条件下的时序依赖。JEPA-Tuner 提出预测式微调框架，用动作条件下的未来预测来正则化 VLA 原生的策略引导，让跨模态引导适配器学会刻画场景与状态在动作下的演化。在异步动作块推理时，预训练预测器可提前预测下一块边界所需引导，使策略无需重叠校正即可预生成并直接执行下一块。在 LIBERO、Meta-World 及真实机器人上，该方法同时提升了同步推理成功率与异步控制性能和平滑度。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate sequences of actions from visual observations, proprioceptive states, and language instructions. In embodied interaction, executing these actions influences subsequent observations and robot states, providing a natural predictive signal for policy learning. However, standard action-supervised fine-tuning does not explicitly capture these action-conditioned temporal dependencies in the guidance consumed by the action predictor. We introduce JEPA-Tuner, a predictive fine-tuning framework that regularizes the VLA's native policy guidance through action-conditioned future prediction. During fine-tuning, a predictor in JEPA-Tuner learns to match guidance encoded from a future observation given the current guidance and committed actions. This objective encourages a cross-modal guidance adapter to capture how the scene and robot state evolve under those actions, while jointly training the action expert on both observed and predicted guidance keeps the representation informative for control. In addition, when deploying the VLA model with asynchronous action-chunk inference, the pre-trained predictor will anticipate the guidance needed at the next chunk boundary. The policy can thus generate the next chunk in advance and execute it from its first action without overlap correction or additional predictor training, enabling efficient and high-quality asynchronous execution. Experiments on LIBERO and Meta-World show that JEPA-Tuner improves task success under synchronous inference with better multi-modal guidance embeddings. For asynchronous control, JEPA-Tuner improves performance and smoothness across different latency settings on both LIBERO simulator and multi-size real robot demonstrations. The project website with video demos is at https://qujx.github.io/JEPA-Tuner-Website.

papers.title_en: $ζ_0$: A Framework for World Action Models with Joint Scene and Body Foresight in Humanoid Control
papers.authors: Yizhi Chen, Zhanxiang Cao, Yitong Wang, Junyu Liu, Hongchu Zeng, Xinyi Peng, Chuxuan Huang, Yicheng Su, Zihao Zhou, Shengcheng Fu, Haoyang Li, Liyun Yan, Tianyue Zhan, Jianming Ma, Yang Zhang, Keqi Zhu, Xiaxi Si, Jinming Yao, Qiao Sun, Shizeng Zhang, Jiangwei Zhong, Yue Gao
papers.evidence: 将视觉-语言-动作策略转化为面向人形控制的世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 针对人形机器人控制中仅靠视觉预见易忽略身体响应的问题，ζ0将视觉-语言-动作策略扩展为世界动作模型，在共享潜在空间中同时预测未来视觉特征与实测关节轨迹。训练时用基于真实未来条件的教师提供参考动作响应，并通过双响应迁移让因果预测器对齐教师与执行策略。在HumanoidArena七项任务和六项真实任务上，分别取得最高79.5%和85.0%成功率，显著超过基线。该框架表明联合场景与身体预见能提升人形机器人动作决策。
papers.abstract_en: World Action Models anticipate visual outcomes to guide robot actions, yet humanoid interaction also depends on how the robot's body responds. Visual foresight alone can miss body motion, while latent-distance losses do not directly supervise action responses. We present $ζ_0$, a framework that turns vision-language-action policies into World Action Models by foreseeing future visual features and measured joint trajectories in a shared latent representation. During training, a teacher conditioned on recorded futures provides a reference action response, and dual-response transfer trains the causal predictor to match it through the teacher and the executing policy. All components are trained jointly, and deployment uses only causally predicted futures. On seven HumanoidArena tasks, $ζ_0$ built on $Ψ_0$ and GR00T N1.7 reaches 63.6% and 79.5% mean success, 18.8 and 9.0 points above these bases. On six real-world tasks, it reaches 78.3% and 85.0%, gains of 16.7 and 10.0 points. On GR00T, its 79.5% tops all compared seven-task joint policies. Project page: https://chenyizhi123.github.io/zeta0-project/

papers.title_en: A2I-VLA: A Two-Stage Vision-Language-Action model with Semantic-Physical Alignment and Integration
papers.authors: Kun Dai, Tianqi Wang, Haibo Lei, Chaoyang Li, Kai Zhang, Fuyuan Qiu, Lijun Zhao, Ruifeng Li, Chuqing Cao, Tao Xie, Wenming Tan
papers.evidence: 融合力触觉感知的两阶段视觉-语言-动作模型
papers.tldr: 视觉观测难以可靠捕捉接触丰富操作中的物理交互信息，而力与触觉信号和视觉语言语义之间存在表征鸿沟。A2I-VLA提出两阶段框架：第一阶段用跨模态对齐损失和分层多模态融合学习语义对齐的力触觉表征，第二阶段通过门控交叉注意力桥接模块将物理特征注入VLA模型以引导动作生成。在三个真实接触丰富任务上，成功率从基线PI05的70%提升到95%。该工作为物理信号与视觉语言语义的深度融合提供了可行范式。
papers.abstract_en: Force and tactile feedback provide essential information about physical interactions in contact-rich manipulation that visual observations alone cannot reliably capture.However, integrating these signals into vision-language-action (VLA) models remains challenging owing to the representational gap between visual-language semantics and physical measurements.To address this challenge, we propose A2I-VLA, a two-stage VLA framework that first learns semantically Aligned force-tactile representations and then Integrates them into a VLA model.In Stage I, a cross-modal alignment loss is introduced to promote correspondence between semantic and physical representations. The tactile and force feature streams are then integrated through a hierarchical multimodal fusion network, and the resulting representations are jointly supervised by future wrench and action prediction losses. The former encourages the model to anticipate physical responses, while the latter associates force-tactile observations with task-relevant manipulation behaviors.In Stage II, a gated cross-attention bridge module adaptively integrates the hierarchical physical features learned in Stage I into the VLA model to guide action generation.Real-world experiments demonstrate that the proposed A2I-VLA significantly outperforms the baseline PI05 across three contact-rich manipulation tasks, improving the success rate from 70% to 95%.

papers.title_en: More Than Picturing the Future: Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Xin Zhang, Yushuo Hou, Anqi Zhao, Moyun Liu, Xingwei Zhao, Bo Tao, Jiawei Du, Joey Tianyi Zhou
papers.evidence: 面向可泛化视觉-语言-动作操作的运动导向隐式推理
papers.tldr: 现有VLA视觉潜在推理虽能低成本替代显式思维链，却把每个潜在对齐到孤立未来帧，容易绑定训练场景外观，场景一变性能就明显下降。本文提出Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning，先由语义潜在确定要完成什么与如何做，再由运动导向潜在按粗到细预测全局场景、交互区域和机器人状态，刻画场景向目标演化的过程。在SimplerEnv-WidowX上，分布内成功率从37.5%升至55.2%，分布外从22.4%升至30.2%；在AgileX Piper双臂平台上，训练场景从60.8%升至90.8%，环境变化下从6.7%升至37.5%。该工作把视觉潜在从“未来帧像什么”转向“动作应如何改变场景”，提升了机器人操作的泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Latent reasoning lets Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models deliberate at a fraction of the cost of explicit chain-of-thought, increasingly through visual foresight, which we show to be indispensable for predicting actions. Yet this paradigm is inherited from Vision-Language Models, where it serves understanding rather than action: each latent is aligned with an isolated future frame, often enriched with further modalities of that frame. We find that this binds the policy to the appearance of its training scenes, so that it degrades sharply once the scene changes. We argue that visual latents for action should capture not what a future frame looks like, but how the scene evolves toward the goal. We therefore propose Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning, which redirects visual latents from the whole frame to the interaction that the action must bring about. Semantic latents, following the stages of embodied chain-of-thought, first establish what to accomplish and how. Conditioned on them, motion-oriented latents anticipate each future step from coarse to fine: from the global scene, to the interaction region spanned by the manipulated object and its destination, to the robot state. Relative to the state-of-the-art latent VLA LaST$_0$, our method raises the mean success rate on SimplerEnv-WidowX from 37.5% to 55.2% in distribution and from 22.4% to 30.2% under out-of-distribution shifts, and on an AgileX Piper dual-arm platform from 60.8% to 90.8% in training scenes and from 6.7% to 37.5% under environmental changes.

papers.title_en: Why Does Sensor Depth Fail Learned Manipulation Policies? Finding the Failure Mode with ACT
papers.authors: Inayat Rasool, Chulwoo Pack, Shabbir Ahmed
papers.evidence: 分析含VLA的RGB-D模仿操作策略失效模式
papers.tldr: 学习型操作策略主要依赖RGB，深度相机的噪声与空洞谁更致命尚不清楚。作者用真实腕部双目相机标定传感器模型，在仿真中分别评估噪声和空洞对三种视觉编码器的RGB-D模仿策略的影响。结果显示完整深度约提升十个百分点，即使噪声达二十倍仍保留大部分增益；而覆盖约六分之一图像的空洞会消除深度收益。策略还受有效性掩码影响，部署时出现空洞可降至仅RGB以下。研究指出深度相机应优先看深度覆盖率而非测量精度。
papers.abstract_en: Learned manipulation policies, from task-specific imitation policies to vision-language-action (VLA) models, rely primarily on RGB images. While some studies report gains from sensor depth, others avoid depth cameras because of measurement noise. Depth cameras introduce both noise and missing depth values (holes), whose relative effects remain unclear. In this study, we calibrate a sensor model using a real wrist-mounted stereo camera and separately evaluate noise and holes on RGB-D imitation policies with three visual encoders in simulation. We found that complete depth improves success by approximately ten percentage points, and most of this gain persists even at twenty times the camera's noise level. In contrast, holes covering about one-sixth of the wrist image eliminate the detectable benefit of depth. The validity mask strongly influences depth reliance: marking a small fraction of pixels as invalid reduces reliance, while filling holes and marking them valid restores most of the benefit. Policies trained on clean depth also lose performance when holes appear only at deployment, sometimes falling below RGB-only performance. These findings suggest that depth cameras for learned policies should therefore be judged by depth coverage more than measurement precision.

papers.title_en: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Vanshaj Khattar, Jing Liu, Toshiaki Koike-Akino, Ming Jin, Ye Wang
papers.evidence: 面向视觉-语言-动作策略的最佳N测试时引导
papers.tldr: 视觉-语言-动作模型部署时常用 best-of-N 测试时引导来提升适应性，但验证器不准确时，增大 N 未必提升性能。作者在 60 个 LIBERO-Safety 任务级案例上，用 π0.5 策略和 MuJoCo 轨迹验证器引入可控误差，考察候选选择偏差。结果显示 N 增大后，被选候选的奖励逐渐偏离准确验证器奖励，出现奖励黑客。验证器校准与 softmax 候选选择可在部分设置缓解该问题。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but adapting to changing environmental conditions still remains challenging. Recent test-time steering methods have shown promise in enabling adaptive VLA policies by utilizing additional computation during deployment. In this paper, we consider best-of-$N$ test-time steering for VLA models, where multiple action candidates are sampled from a fixed policy and a verifier is used to select the best one during deployment. We show that increasing $N$ does not always improve performance when the verifier is inaccurate, and can favor candidates whose scores exploit prediction errors, a form of reward hacking. We study this effect on 60 LIBERO-Safety task-level cases using a $π_{0.5}$ policy, with ten repetitions per case. We introduce controlled errors in a MuJoCo trajectory verifier and show that as $N$ increases, selected candidate rewards diverge from the accurate verifier rewards, leading to reward hacking. We also show that verifier calibration and softmax-based candidate selection can mitigate reward hacking in some settings.

papers.title_en: $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM: Efficient Hierarchical Memory Across Modalities and Timescales for World-Action Models
papers.authors: Xiaopeng Zhang, Weiqi Yuan, Xin Zhu, Jiaxi Huang, Yueqi Hu, Yin Zhang, Jian Yao, Yanjie Li
papers.evidence: 面向长程机器人操作的分层记忆世界-动作模型
papers.tldr: 长时程机器人操作依赖历史，但视觉历史存储检索成本高、压缩易丢细节，动作历史又含互补行为信息。M²-WAM 为世界动作模型引入分层视觉与交互记忆：短期保留密集观测，长期以门控 delta 更新维护固定大小关联记忆，并将动作前缀编码为紧凑时序表示；经逐层检索融合，在线内存有界且不随回合增长。在 MIKASA-Robo 和 RMBench 上平均成功率较 Fast-WAM 绝对提升 53.2% 和 61.2%，真实任务较 LingBot-VA 提升 29.3%。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires historical context, yet retaining extensive visual histories incurs growing storage and retrieval costs, while aggressive compression risks losing fine-grained information needed for subsequent decisions. Moreover, executed action histories capture intermediate behaviors that sparse visual observations may miss. Preserving this complementary context efficiently calls for modality-specific memory mechanisms that balance recent detail with long-term retention. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM, a world-action model equipped with hierarchical visual and interaction memories. $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM preserves recent visual observations in dense short-term memory while consolidating entries evicted from this window into fixed-size associative long-term memory through gated delta updates. Within the same short- and long-term hierarchy, interaction memory encodes executed action prefixes into compact temporal representations, complementing visual observations with behavioral context. These complementary memories are integrated into world-action modeling through layer-wise retrieval, enabling memory-augmented action generation with a bounded online memory footprint independent of episode length. On the memory-dependent simulation benchmarks MIKASA-Robo and RMBench, $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves +53.2% and +61.2% absolute improvements in average success rates over Fast-WAM, respectively. These gains extend to real-world manipulation, where $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves a +29.3% absolute improvement over LingBot-VA in average success across three tasks. These results suggest that $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM offers a promising approach to efficient memory-augmented world-action modeling.

papers.title_en: DriftWAM: Faster World-Action Models via Action-Aware Video Drifting
papers.authors: Minyang Li, Siyu Xu, Yunke Wang, Ying-Cong Chen, Chang Xu, Daochang Liu
papers.evidence: 通过动作感知视频蒸馏的高效少步世界动作模型用于机器人控制
papers.tldr: 世界动作模型需迭代去噪，推理开销大；现有轨迹一致性蒸馏偏重视觉保真，未利用下游动作信息。DriftWAM将预测视频诱导的动作引入视频学习，通过动作感知视频漂移与动作引导正则实现少步蒸馏。在RoboTwin 2.0、LIBERO及真实机器人任务中，同推理速度下少步设置持续优于先前方法。该工作提升了少步世界动作模型的部署效率与任务性能。
papers.abstract_en: World-action models (WAMs) unify future video prediction and action generation for robotic control, but their reliance on iterative denoising incurs substantial inference costs. Distilling these models into few-step generators offers a promising route to efficient deployment, yet maintaining task performance under aggressive step reduction remains challenging. Existing methods rely on point-wise trajectory consistency distillation, which pursues high visual fidelity while leaving downstream action information unexploited in optimizing video generation, and also lacks explicit distribution-level alignment. To address this, we propose DriftWAM, a few-step WAM distillation framework that incorporates the actions induced by predicted videos into video learning. Specifically, DriftWAM integrates action-aware video drifting, which performs video distribution matching through a joint visual--action similarity kernel to steer sample evolution under the guidance of these induced actions, with action-guided video regularization, which leverages the compatible teacher--student matches identified by the joint kernel to backpropagate action-level gradients directly into the video generator. Evaluations on the RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO benchmarks, as well as in real-world robotic manipulation tasks, show that DriftWAM consistently outperforms prior consistency distillation methods across few-step settings at the same inference speed.

papers.title_en: JetDiffusion: Pushing the Speed Limits of Video Generation with NVFP4 Sparse Attention
papers.authors: Yulun Wu, Zihan Min, Minshen Zhang, Kaiqin Kong, Ji Xie, Will Lin, Junda Chen, Wenxuan Tan, Aryan Kumar, Loay Rashid, Qingyu Yin, Hao Zhang
papers.evidence: 结合自定义推理内核的低比特NVFP4量化注意力
papers.tldr: 长序列注意力是视频生成的主要计算瓶颈，稀疏与低比特量化虽能加速，但难以联合适配。JetDiffusion基于可训练视频稀疏量化注意力VSQA，结合原生NVFP4计算与算子融合推理内核，并配合线性量化和步蒸馏。在90%稀疏度下，VSQA较FlashAttention加速8-29倍；Wan2.1-14B在RTX 5090上实现273倍端到端加速且画质相当。该工作提出可稳定适配量化、稀疏与少步去噪的分阶段训练方案，推动视频生成速度极限。
papers.abstract_en: Attention over long sequences is a major computational bottleneck in video generation, which can be alleviated through sparsity and low-bit quantization. We propose JetDiffusion, a video generation system built on trainable Video Sparse Quantized Attention (VSQA), with custom inference kernels that combine native NVFP4 computation and kernel fusion. At 90% sparsity, VSQA accelerates attention by 8-29x compared with FlashAttention on different hardwares. To further accelerate video generation, we combine VSQA with NVFP4 linear quantization and step distillation. Although each technique can individually preserve generation quality, jointly adapting to all three remains challenging, particularly under aggressive NVFP4 quantization. Through empirical studies, we develop an effective staged training recipe that enables stable adaptation to quantization, sparsity, and few-step denoising. On Wan2.1-14B, the resulting model achieves 273x end-to-end video generation speedup on the RTX 5090 while maintaining comparable video quality.

papers.title_en: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Xu Yang, Kailai Sun, Qianchuan Zhao
papers.evidence: 用于机器人操作中动作比较的反事实世界模型
papers.tldr: 机器人操作中，世界模型能预测动作结果，却难以在同一物理情境下比较不同动作的个体效应及切换风险。WhatIf 以共享潜在物理与转移噪声耦合候选未来，并用动作诱导的稀疏对象因子因果图约束反事实推演。基于此，CAP 在共享情境中按相对优势排序计划并限制伤害概率。配对仿真干预显示其在反事实精度、因果图恢复、组合泛化与决策质量上的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: World models predict what happens under an action, but choosing between actions requires comparing their outcomes in the same physical situation. Factual transitions alone determine action-wise marginal futures and average effects, but not individual effects or the probability that switching actions causes harm. We introduce WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for manipulation that couples candidate futures through shared latent physics and transition noise inferred from factual history. Each candidate action induces a sparse object-factor causal graph describing the physical pathways it activates. Rolling out these graphs under the shared situation anchors predictions to observed outcomes and confines action contrasts to the objects each action reaches. Shared type-conditioned functions support varying numbers of objects, while a round-trip loss enforces action-invariant abduction without counterfactual labels. We show that replacing an individual effect with its conditional mean incurs mean-squared error equal to its conditional variance, motivating comparisons between coupled futures. Building on these comparisons, Counterfactual Advantage Planning (CAP) ranks plans by their advantage over an incumbent within shared situations and constrains the probability of harm. Paired advantages reduce estimator variance by a factor of $1-ρ$, where $ρ$ is the correlation between branch outcomes, and cancel model errors shared by both branches. Each executed transition provides hindsight advantages to update the physics posterior, the next plan, and an amortized policy without a learned critic. We further establish when observational transitions identify interventional dynamics. Paired simulator interventions evaluate counterfactual accuracy, graph recovery, compositional generalization, and decision quality.

papers.title_en: FlipVLA: Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action(VLA) Models Only Through Bit Flips
papers.authors: Zexi Zhao, Zizhen Liu, Jing Justin Ye, Huawei Li
papers.evidence: 通过比特翻转对生成机器人动作的视觉-语言-动作模型实施后门攻击
papers.tldr: VLA模型直接驱动机器人动作，参数被恶意篡改会威胁物理安全。FlipVLA研究不重训练、仅用少量固定比特翻转植入对象触发后门。方法以FC-GELU-FC中的选择器-放大器两阶段构造触发响应并放大为动作扰动。在OpenVLA-OFT与GR00T N1.7、四个LIBERO套件上攻击成功率达90.22%–100%，干净场景任务成功率最多降1.5个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions in real-world environments, making malicious model tampering a potential threat to physical safety. We study whether object-triggered backdoors can be implanted through a small, fixed set of parameter bit flips without retraining. The central challenge is to make persistent weight modifications disrupt trigger-present behavior while preserving performance on non-trigger inputs. We propose FlipVLA, a two-stage selector-amplifier method that exploits existing visual features within an FC-GELU-FC structure. The selector constructs a trigger-dependent response in a selected channel, using GELU to attenuate background activity. The amplifier modifies a connected downstream weight to convert this response into an action-relevant perturbation. Channel screening and discrete bit search construct both components under a limited modification budget. Experiments on OpenVLA-OFT and GR00T N1.7 across four LIBERO suites achieve attack success rates of 90.22% to 100%, with task success decreasing by at most 1.5 percentage points on clean scenes.

papers.title_en: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
papers.authors: Zhiyue Zhao, Mingyu Liu, Bolin Zhang, Liyang Li, Guangyu Huang, Canyu Zhao, Jinchuan Shi, Haokai Zhang, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen
papers.evidence: 在失败情形下失准的机器人操作世界模型
papers.tldr: 机器人世界模型常依赖成功演示，抓取错位或滑落等失败场景预测会失效，甚至不如静态基线。作者构建62k条扰动抓取仿真轨迹，提出WorldReforge，用交互对齐与表面对应两种训练信号强化失败物理。在Cosmos3 Nano上，物体轨迹误差总体降低28.2%，未见物体降低35.0%，动作结果差异预测误差降低43.3%。该方法无需额外推理成本，并迁移到DROID与真实失败视频。
papers.abstract_en: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at aim-uofa.github.io/WorldReforge/.
